notes: The stack cannot be handed from one Legion role to the next: stack.sh identifies its processes by the pids in $LOADTEST_ROOT/run/*.pid, and each role of a pod has its own PID namespace, so the implementer's Postgres (pid 8228 in pid:[17]) was invisible to me (pid:[27]) and `check_port` refused my first run with 'port 35432 ... is already in use by a process that is not this stack's; free it or set LOADTEST_PG_PORT'. The implementer ran `stack.sh stop` for me over Envoy and I started the stack in my own namespace. Not a failure of an acceptance criterion; worth a line in the README's 'One run at a time' section.

summary.json flags saturation and the idle cores before the window, but nothing records what else ran on the box during the window, although samples.json holds it (sys_busy_ticks and every stack process's cpu_ticks). In t-base, 19,571 of the window's 231,233 busy ticks were no stack process's; in base-1, 2,861 of 147,572. On a Legion pod six roles share the two cores, so a sibling role's work can inflate a measurement with nothing in summary.json to show it.
